domain_reasoning: Most time goes into writing scripts, emailing participants and setting up accounts and access, which is document and message work.
length_reasoning: A small round with a few known participants and reused scripts takes under two hours; a larger third-party round with new scripts, environments and many accounts takes most of a day or more.
review_reasoning: The manager reads the plan, scripts and schedule and checks access works for a few participants; a typical round needs scripts read against scope.
stakes_reasoning: Bad scripts or missing access waste participants' time and delay the round, but it is fixable and visible quickly.
context_reasoning: Needs knowledge of the product, its test environments and who the participants are, built over weeks.

unit_flag_reason: Task mixes workflow analysis, space design and cost comparison, and a support specialist's feasibility study is broad, but items are coded as a single report.
domain_reasoning: The study consists of gathering information, analysing workflows and writing a report with a recommendation, mostly reading and writing.
length_reasoning: A small study of one office process takes a day or so; a multi-department study with space design and cost comparison takes several days of active work.
review_reasoning: A manager must read the whole report, check the assumptions and cost figures and judge the recommendation.
stakes_reasoning: A poor recommendation can lead to a costly wrong purchase or rework, though it is usually caught before commitment.
context_reasoning: Needs knowledge of the organisation's workflows, staff and budgets, learned over weeks to months.

domain_reasoning: Apart from talking, the time goes into looking up product or service information in knowledge bases and account systems.
length_reasoning: A simple question is answered in a couple of minutes; a detailed product question with lookups takes ten or more.
review_reasoning: A QA reviewer listens to the recording, often at speed, and checks the answer against the knowledge base.
stakes_reasoning: A wrong answer misleads a customer and may cause a complaint or return, but can be corrected on a later contact.
context_reasoning: Needs the employer's products, policies and knowledge base, which take weeks to learn.

domain_reasoning: Beyond talking, the time goes into having the case notes and claim or inquiry results open in the claims or CRM system.
length_reasoning: A short callback delivering a simple result takes a few minutes; explaining a claim adjustment and answering questions takes ten to fifteen.
review_reasoning: A reviewer listens to the recorded call and compares what was said to the claim record.
stakes_reasoning: Misstated claim results or adjustments can cause disputes or regulatory complaints and are harder to reverse once communicated.
context_reasoning: Needs the employer's claims process, adjustment rules and case history, learned over weeks.

domain_reasoning: The work is reading the build's behaviour from notes and writing up findings and recommendations as text.
length_reasoning: A short note on one feature takes about half an hour; a thorough note on a large build with screenshots and repro steps takes a couple of hours.
review_reasoning: A developer or product owner reads the note and reproduces a few of the points to confirm they are accurate.
stakes_reasoning: A wrong or unclear note wastes developer time or misdirects a fix, caught in later testing.
context_reasoning: Needs familiarity with the product and its conventions, picked up over weeks.

domain_reasoning: Time goes into checking monitoring tools, system consoles and logs and updating the ticket.
length_reasoning: Many alerts are transient or known and closed in minutes; a real performance problem can take an hour or more to trace.
review_reasoning: A supervisor reads the closing note and glances at the metrics; a typical one needs the cause checked against logs.
stakes_reasoning: A wrongly closed alert usually recurs and is caught, but a missed fault can cause an outage.
context_reasoning: Telling noise from a real problem needs months of knowing this environment's normal behaviour.

domain_reasoning: Most of the time goes into operating and configuring a tracker tool: fields, workflows, permissions.
length_reasoning: A simple tracker from a template takes a couple of hours; a configured custom workflow with fields, permissions and migration takes a couple of days.
review_reasoning: A manager needs to open the configuration, walk through fields and workflows and try creating a defect.
stakes_reasoning: A badly configured tracker causes rework and confusion for the team but can be changed later.
context_reasoning: Needs the team's process, defect lifecycle and existing tools, learned over weeks.

domain_reasoning: The work is running commands and operating the machine or application to check it works, then noting the ticket.
length_reasoning: A quick check after a routine install takes a few minutes; verifying a complex repair or system change takes half an hour.
review_reasoning: A lead reads the ticket note and checks it lists the tests done; a typical item may need a spot check on the machine.
stakes_reasoning: A missed fault returns as a reopened ticket and annoyed user, cheap to fix.
context_reasoning: A skilled outsider could run standard checks, but local software and configuration take some weeks to learn.

domain_reasoning: Beyond talking, the time goes into entering complaint details into the complaint or CRM system.
length_reasoning: A simple complaint is captured in about five minutes; a complicated one with account lookup and several details takes fifteen.
review_reasoning: A reviewer listens to the recording and checks the captured record for completeness.
stakes_reasoning: Missing or wrong details cause rework for investigators and a repeat contact, and a mishandled complaint may escalate.
context_reasoning: Needs the employer's complaint categories, policies and systems, learned over weeks.

domain_reasoning: The work is operating test tools, triggering runs and logging results in the test management tool.
length_reasoning: An automated run is triggered and logged in minutes; a manual run with many steps and failure notes takes an hour or more.
review_reasoning: A lead checks the logged results against the run, with a few failed cases opened to confirm the evidence.
stakes_reasoning: A wrongly recorded result may hide a defect until later, though it is usually caught by the next run.
context_reasoning: Needs the team's test suites, tool setup and conventions, learned over weeks.

domain_reasoning: The work is reviewing customer contact records and writing a recommendation with examples.
length_reasoning: A short recommendation from known recurring cases takes an hour or so; one needing data pulled and several examples takes half a day.
review_reasoning: A supervisor reads the recommendation and checks the examples support the claim.
stakes_reasoning: A weak recommendation is usually ignored or sent back, with little direct loss.
context_reasoning: Needs the employer's processes and the history of customer issues, built over weeks to months.

domain_reasoning: The curation pass means working in the defect tracker: merging, updating statuses and adding workarounds.
length_reasoning: A small pass over a few dozen records takes an hour or two; a pre-release pass over hundreds takes most of a day.
review_reasoning: A lead samples merges and status changes and checks workarounds, which takes substantial reading.
stakes_reasoning: Wrong merges or workarounds mislead support and developers but can be corrected.
context_reasoning: Needs deep familiarity with the product's defect history, which takes months.

domain_reasoning: Time goes into reading the ticket, looking up solutions and replying, using ticketing and knowledge tools.
length_reasoning: A routine question is answered in about ten minutes; a hard one requiring research or reproduction takes an hour.
review_reasoning: A lead reads the question and answer, and checks the instructions are correct.
stakes_reasoning: Wrong instructions reach a user and cause a repeat ticket or small damage, but can be reversed.
context_reasoning: Needs the company's standard software, hardware and local conventions, learned over weeks.

domain_reasoning: Apart from talking, the time goes into looking at the application, logs and the customer's environment.
length_reasoning: A quick diagnosis takes ten minutes; a hard problem with reproduction and screen sharing takes an hour.
review_reasoning: A reviewer replays or reads notes of the session and checks the cause fits the symptoms, which takes close to its length.
stakes_reasoning: A wrong diagnosis misdirects a customer or developers, wasting time but reversible.
context_reasoning: Needs knowledge of the product and customer environments, built over months.

domain_reasoning: The work is in the defect tracker and the build, retesting the fix and updating the ticket.
length_reasoning: A simple fix is checked in ten minutes; a complex fix requiring environment setup and regression checks takes an hour.
review_reasoning: A lead reads the ticket note and repeats a quick check of the fix.
stakes_reasoning: A fix wrongly closed will resurface in production or later, causing rework.
context_reasoning: Needs the product's behaviour and test environments, learned over weeks.

domain_reasoning: Most time goes into entering the request into the contract, address or account system.
length_reasoning: A simple address change takes five minutes; a contract form with verification takes twenty or more.
review_reasoning: A reviewer compares the entered order with the written request and the confirmation.
stakes_reasoning: A wrong order or discontinuance affects billing and service, and may cause financial loss to customer or employer.
context_reasoning: Needs the employer's forms, systems and rules, learned over weeks.

domain_reasoning: The work is operating vendor portals or email to open a case and updating the ticket with warranty details.
length_reasoning: A simple warranty referral takes fifteen minutes; a complicated case with diagnostics and warranty checks takes an hour.
review_reasoning: A supervisor checks the case, warranty details and ticket note, which are short.
stakes_reasoning: A bad referral delays repair and may void warranty coverage, but is usually correctable.
context_reasoning: Needs the company's vendors, assets and warranty records, learned over weeks.
